title: Resumind
shortDescription: Full-stack AI web app that analyzes your CV, returns an ATS score and detailed per-category feedback calibrated on the target job description.
fullDescription: Resumind lets you upload your CV as a PDF, specify the target job description, and receive a detailed AI analysis: ATS score, tone & style, content, structure, and skills — each with practical suggestions labeled as strengths or areas to improve.
problem: Tailoring a CV for each job application is time-consuming and hard to evaluate objectively. Resumind solves this with structured AI feedback calibrated on the specific role, giving actionable scores and tips instead of generic advice.
features: AI feedback across 5 categories (ATS, Tone & Style, Content, Structure, Skills) with 0–100 scores
Client-side PDF→PNG conversion at 4x scale using PDF.js from CDN
Split-view layout: sticky CV preview on the left, scrollable feedback on the right
Google OAuth via better-auth with per-user analysis limit (max 3)
stackSummary: React Router v7 with SSR, PostgreSQL via Drizzle ORM, Google OAuth with better-auth, AI via DeepSeek Chat API, client-side PDF rendering with PDF.js.
whatILearned: Handling binary files (bytea) on PostgreSQL and serving blobs via a REST API without a dedicated filesystem.
Converting PDF to canvas to PNG at high resolution client-side using PDF.js loaded from CDN.
Structuring AI prompts to get consistent JSON output using response_format: json_object on DeepSeek.
Protecting routes with SSR loaders in React Router v7 (server-side redirect when unauthenticated).
Migrating an architecture from a KV store (Puter.js) to a relational database while keeping the same Zustand interface.
Configuring better-auth with drizzleAdapter for Google OAuth without email/password.

particularAspects.title: Filesystem abstraction
particularAspects.content: The Zustand usePuterStore abstraction simulates a virtual filesystem (upload, read, delete) over a custom REST API — originally built for Puter.js, then migrated to PostgreSQL without changing component code.

particularAspects.title: High-res conversion
particularAspects.content: PDF conversion uses a canvas at scale 4 to produce a high-resolution preview that is saved as a PNG in the database.

particularAspects.title: Structured AI feedback
particularAspects.content: AI feedback is structured across 5 categories (ATS, Tone & Style, Content, Structure, Skills) with a 0–100 score and tips labeled as 'good' or 'improve'.

particularAspects.title: Split-view layout
particularAspects.content: Split-view sticky layout: CV preview on the left, scrollable feedback on the right — optimized for desktop.

designFocus: SVG score gauge with linear pink→blue gradient and strokeDashoffset animation.
Conditional color badges: green/yellow/red based on score thresholds (70/50).
Fade-in transitions on feedback and image preview using animate-in duration-1000.
Decorative SVG background on all main pages.
Loading state with animated GIF during CV scanning.
developmentFocus: SSR with React Router v7: server-side loaders and actions for auth, DB queries, and redirects.
Drizzle schema with ai_resume_ prefix on all tables to coexist with other schemas in the same database.
RESTful API routes for files and resumes with session cookie authentication.
PDF.js loaded lazily from CDN with singleton pattern and loadPromise lock to prevent multiple loads.
Dockerfile for containerized deployment on any cloud platform.
interactionDetails: Drag-and-drop PDF upload via react-dropzone with immediate file preview.
Form with company name, job title, and job description to personalize the AI analysis.
Progressive feedback via animated statusMessage across upload → conversion → analysis → save phases.
Clickable CV preview link that opens the original PDF in a new tab.
Protected navigation: automatic redirect to /auth with a next param to return to the original page after login.
technicalHighlights: DeepSeek Chat API with response_format: { type: 'json_object' } for structured, directly parseable AI output.
PDF→PNG conversion via canvas API in the browser (4x scale, imageSmoothingQuality: high) with no server-side dependencies.
Files stored as bytea on PostgreSQL — no external object storage required.
better-auth configured with drizzleAdapter and Google provider: zero password management.
Zustand store as a filesystem abstraction layer — enabled migration from Puter.js to a custom API without touching components.
portfolioValue: Demonstrates the ability to integrate multiple complex layers in a single app: OAuth, structured AI output, client-side PDF processing, relational DB storage, and SSR. The architecture went through at least two significant migrations (KV→PostgreSQL, Puter→custom API), showing refactoring ability without regressions.

suggestedCaseStudyText.overview: Resumind is a web app that lets you upload your CV as a PDF, specify a target job description, and receive a detailed AI analysis: ATS score, tone & style, content, structure, and skills — each with practical tips labeled as strengths or areas to improve.
suggestedCaseStudyText.learnings: The project required tackling several non-trivial problems in parallel: PDF-to-image conversion in the browser without a server, structuring AI prompts for reliable JSON output, and managing binary files on PostgreSQL. The most interesting part was building a filesystem abstraction layer on Zustand that made the migration from Puter.js to a custom API completely transparent to the components.
suggestedCaseStudyText.particularAspects: The architecture went through at least two migration cycles during development — from SQLite to PostgreSQL and from an external KV store to files on DB. In both cases the public interface of the components stayed unchanged, thanks to the Zustand abstraction that simulates filesystem operations. PDF conversion happens entirely client-side at 4x scale to ensure a high-resolution preview.
suggestedCaseStudyText.outcome: The result is a working full-stack app with Google authentication, AI analysis personalized per job description, per-user usage limits, and a split-view layout optimized for comparing the CV with its feedback. Ready for containerized deployment via Docker.

title: Monoforge Studio
shortDescription: Official website of Monoforge, a technical-visual lab that designs direct AI systems, automations and conversational interfaces.
fullDescription: Monoforge is the official website of a technical-visual lab specializing in direct AI systems. It is not a landing page: it is a complete web product that includes animated sections, service pages, solutions, blog insights and an integrated AI assistant.
problem: Building a studio website requires more than a landing page template. The challenge is to deliver a complete product experience: a sophisticated design system, a stateful AI chatbot integrated seamlessly, production-grade rate limiting and custom shaders that communicate visual brand identity without compromising performance.
features: AI Assistant with XState state machine
Custom GLSL shaders and shared WebGL renderer
Multi-layer rate limiting with Redis
Dark design system with Klein blue and glassmorphism
stackSummary: Next.js with App Router for routing and SSR, Three.js for shaders and 3D geometries, XState for stateful chatbot AI management, Redis for distributed rate limiting. The stack merges advanced visual frontend with robust backend API.
whatILearned: How to build a shared WebGL singleton renderer to reduce GPU overhead when multiple components use shaders concurrently
Managing complex state machines with XState 5 for a chatbot with rate limiting, intent detection, email handoff, and Turnstile anti-bot
Integrating DeepSeek API with a multi-layer rate limiting system via Upstash Redis on Next.js API routes
How to structure a scalable design system with custom CSS tokens, border opacity scale, and consistent Klein blue glassmorphism
Performance optimization with dynamic imports for below-the-fold 3D components, custom profiling hooks, and controlled lazy loading

particularAspects.title: AI concierge
particularAspects.content: Monica, the site's AI assistant, uses XState as the state machine and DeepSeek v4-flash as the model, with precise prompt engineering for CTAs, conversational flow, and brand tone

particularAspects.title: GLSL shaders
particularAspects.content: Custom GLSL shader system for animated backgrounds with water plane treatment and shared singleton renderer across multiple instances

particularAspects.title: Hero logo shader
particularAspects.content: Interactive hero logo with Three.js: custom fragment shader with glow, UV distortion, and real-time pointer tracking

particularAspects.title: Icon dither effects
particularAspects.content: Dither shader effect for EngineTimeline icons with three modes: halftone, bayer, and crosshatch

designFocus: Design system centered on International Klein Blue (#002FA7) with dark backgrounds (#020b1a) and metallic glass card effects
Precise visual hierarchy with two base rays, border opacity scale white/10-white/70, and coherent glass surfaces
Scroll reveal animations with Framer Motion: word-by-word reveal, stagger animations, and InView fade
Coherent motion design with timeline animations, card stagger, hero typing effect, and confetti canvas for conversions
developmentFocus: Chat state machine with XState with distinct states: idle, typing, success, rate_limited, error, report_pending, and granular notice system
Chat API route with conversation history context, intent/stage/confidence detection, and structured response with CTA actions
Shared WebGL renderer singleton for shader backgrounds, useful for reducing overhead from multiple instances on mobile and parallel sections
Modular CSS architecture with design tokens in variables.css, separate components per section, and dedicated utilities
interactionDetails: Hero logo shader with mouse tracking, UV distortion, and real-time glow via Three.js pointer uniform
EngineTimeline with synchronized scroll progress, sequential card reveal on desktop and mobile card stack
CampaignShowcase with parallax scrolling via custom useScrollProgress and useCardHeight hooks
Animated chat widget with AnimatePresence: smooth open/close, typing indicator, and countdown timer for rate limit
technicalHighlights: DeepSeek v4-flash as the chat model, chosen for reduced latency and low cost on short discovery conversations
Cloudflare Turnstile integrated in the client-side chat widget, with server-side validation in the API route for every message
Email submission limit separate from IP rate limit and tracked on Redis with daily TTL to protect the lead handoff flow
Dynamic sitemap generated via Next.js and OG image generated programmatically on /og route with title/subtitle parameters
portfolioValue: The project demonstrates the ability to build an end-to-end studio website with high visual quality and an operational integrated AI system. It's not a demo: it includes a chatbot with state machine, production-grade rate limiting, custom shaders, documented design system, and scalable architecture.

suggestedCaseStudyText.overview: Monoforge is the official website of a technical-visual lab specializing in direct AI systems. It's not a landing page: it's a complete web product that includes animated sections, service pages, solutions, blog insights, and an integrated AI assistant. The site is built on Next.js 16 with App Router, React 19, and a stack combining Three.js, XState, Framer Motion, and Tailwind CSS 4. Every visual component has a precise technical counterpart: from GLSL shaders to Redis rate limits, from CSS token systems to the chatbot state machine.
suggestedCaseStudyText.learnings: The main challenge was integrating a stateful AI chatbot into a premium visual experience without compromising performance or conversational flow control. XState made all possible states explicit: rate limit, error, handoff, and report. The shared WebGL singleton renderer solved the GPU overhead problem with multiple active shader instances. The multi-layer rate limiting system taught how to design realistic defenses on public APIs without blocking legitimate users.
suggestedCaseStudyText.particularAspects: Monica, the site's assistant, uses DeepSeek v4-flash with a system prompt that defines tone, CTA rules, flow, and edge-case behaviors. The hero logo's fragment shader handles UV distortion, glow, and real-time pointer tracking via Three.js uniform. The EngineTimeline combines custom scroll progress with dither shader in three modes for icons — a technical-visual detail requiring coordination between CSS, canvas, and React state.
suggestedCaseStudyText.outcome: The result is a site that works as both a marketing asset and a direct demonstration of Monoforge's capabilities: integrated AI, advanced visual engineering, clean architecture. In the portfolio it shows that a single developer can govern the entire stack, from GLSL to Redis, with visual and technical coherence.

title: Colivio
shortDescription: Fullstack coliving platform with hybrid AI search (vector + SQL), Stripe payments, JWT authentication and admin panel. An end-to-end project covering frontend, backend, database and external integrations.
fullDescription: Colivio is a fullstack coliving platform built with Next.js 14, Prisma and PostgreSQL. The goal was to cover the entire stack of a real product: JWT authentication with RBAC, booking with race condition handling, Stripe payments with webhooks, and an AI search that interprets natural language queries.
problem: Finding a coliving space that matches specific requirements — location, budget, amenities, vibe — is hard without intelligent search. Colivio solves this with a hybrid AI search engine that combines semantic similarity (pgvector) with structured SQL filters, interpreting natural language queries and falling back gracefully when no exact match is found.
features: Hybrid AI search engine: natural language input parsed via function calling, then vector + SQL query on pgvector with weighted scoring (60% vector, 30% keyword, 10% exact match)
Progressive search fallback: automatically relaxes budget by 20% and removes city filter when no exact results found, communicating the change to the user
Booking flow with availability check, dynamic pricing calculation and integrated Stripe payment
RBAC with 4 roles (Guest, Host, Admin, Superadmin), JWT middleware and resource ownership verification on every route
Admin panel with audit log, statistics and user management
GDPR compliance: data export and account deletion with personal data anonymization
stackSummary: Next.js 14 fullstack with App Router, Prisma on PostgreSQL, Stripe for payments, OpenAI for vector embeddings and semantic search, Zustand for client-side state management.
whatILearned: How to implement a hybrid search that combines vector similarity (pgvector) with structured SQL filters and keyword matching, assigning different weights to each component (60% vector, 30% keyword, 10% exact match).
Handling race conditions in bookings with serializable transactions and optimistic locking (version field on the Booking model).
End-to-end Stripe integration: Payment Intents, webhook signature verification, idempotency, refunds and dispute handling.
How to structure RBAC (4 roles: Guest, Host, Admin, Superadmin) with JWT middleware and resource ownership verification on every route.
Systematic audit logging for all critical actions — essential for GDPR and compliance.
The gap between a 'working' backend and a production-ready one: that 20% made of job queues, graceful shutdown, monitoring, backup strategy, CSRF protection.

particularAspects.title: Hybrid search
particularAspects.content: The AI search is not a simple chatbot: it extracts structured criteria from the natural language conversation via function calling, then runs a hybrid vector+SQL query on pgvector, with automatic fallback to a relaxed search (budget +20%, city filter removed) if no results are found.

particularAspects.title: Honest README
particularAspects.content: The backend README explicitly lists what is missing for production — a deliberate choice to document limitations instead of hiding them. It makes the project honest and pedagogically interesting.

particularAspects.title: Design system
particularAspects.content: The custom Tailwind design system includes a warm/neutral palette (bg #FAFAF7, accent #C8553D) with Fraunces (serif display) + DM Sans font pairing, animations with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) easing and spring, and skeleton loaders with shimmer effect.

particularAspects.title: Prisma schema
particularAspects.content: Very complete Prisma schema: immutable pricing snapshot on bookings, custom per-date pricing, nightly/weekly/monthly rates, Stripe Connect support for host payouts, GDPR anonymization, 4 booking status enums.

designFocus: Warm-neutral palette with terracotta accent (#C8553D) and olive (#5C6B4F), consistent with the coliving lifestyle aesthetic.
Editorial font pairing: Fraunces (serif) for headings, DM Sans for body — conveys a premium tone without feeling cold.
Hero section with full-bleed image, multi-layer gradient overlay and animated 'Spaces available now' badge with pulsing green dot.
Custom CSS animations (fadeUp, scaleIn, slideIn, shimmer) with non-linear easing for fluid feedback.
Skeleton loaders with shimmer effect for all listing cards during loading.
Semantic status badges with differentiated colors (confirmed green, pending orange, cancelled red, refunded blue).
developmentFocus: Next.js 14 App Router with Route Groups for auth and dashboard, clear separation between Server Components and Client Components.
Internal REST API pattern with typed route handlers, structured error handling and no stack trace leaks in production.
Zustand for client-side auth state, TanStack Query for listing fetching/caching.
Input validation with Zod on auth and forms, react-hook-form for form UX.
Prisma with $queryRaw for the pgvector vector query (not supported by the standard ORM), then hydration of relations with a second Prisma query.
Next.js middleware for route protection based on role.
interactionDetails: AI Search Widget: natural language input that shows listing cards directly in the chat, with matching reasons (e.g. 'Near the sea', 'Within budget €750/month').
Progressive search fallback: if no exact results, the query automatically relaxes budget by 20% and removes the city constraint, communicating it to the user.
Booking flow with availability check, dynamic price calculation (nights × rate + cleaning + service fee) and integrated Stripe payment.
Admin panel with audit log, statistics and user management with RBAC.
technicalHighlights: Hybrid search engine: pgvector for cosine similarity, SQL WHERE for hard filters (budget, city, coworking), keyword mapping for features/vibes with weighted boosting.
Optimistic locking with version field on the Booking model to prevent concurrent double-bookings.
Stripe webhook with HMAC signature verification and idempotency — handles payment intents, refunds and disputes.
Dual architecture: same domain implemented both in Next.js App Router and standalone Express (for comparison).
OpenAI embedding generation for each listing at seed time, runtime query embedding for each search.
GDPR: data export and account deletion with personal data anonymization.
portfolioValue: Demonstrates the ability to design and implement a complex end-to-end system: from the data schema (Prisma/PostgreSQL) to external integrations (Stripe, OpenAI), through to the frontend (Next.js, custom design system). The standout feature is the hybrid AI search, a non-trivial pattern that combines semantic search with structured queries. The honest README about production limitations shows technical maturity.

suggestedCaseStudyText.overview: Colivio is a fullstack coliving platform built with Next.js 14, Prisma and PostgreSQL. The idea was to cover the entire stack of a real product: JWT authentication with RBAC, booking with race condition handling, Stripe payments with webhooks, and an AI search that interprets requests in natural language.
suggestedCaseStudyText.learnings: The most interesting part was building the hybrid search engine: instead of choosing between semantic search (pgvector) and SQL filters, I combined both with calibrated weights. I learned that the hard part isn't making the code work — it's understanding what's missing for production reliability: job queues, graceful shutdown, monitoring, backup. I explicitly documented that missing 20%.
suggestedCaseStudyText.particularAspects: Two choices I'm proud of: the automatic search fallback (if no exact results, it expands budget and geography communicating it to the user) and the warm design system with Fraunces+DM Sans, built to convey a consistent lifestyle aesthetic without external libraries.
suggestedCaseStudyText.outcome: A working concept product that covers the patterns of a real application: auth, booking, payments, AI search, admin panel. Useful as a technical reference and as a demonstration of how to design a complex system before deploying it.

title: InterSpeak
shortDescription: AI-powered voice interview practice platform simulating real job interviews across 50+ roles and 6 industries — with real-time feedback, written sessions, and a credit-based subscription.
fullDescription: InterSpeak is an AI voice interview coach that lets users practice job interviews across 50+ roles and 6 industries. Users select a role and difficulty, then speak directly with an AI interviewer in real time via WebRTC. The platform supports dual session modes (voice and written), live mid-interview feedback, and structured post-session analysis — all gated behind a credit-based subscription.
problem: Practicing job interviews without a human partner is hard: generic AI chatbots lack role specificity, realistic voice dynamics, and structured feedback. InterSpeak addresses this with a real-time voice AI, adaptive difficulty, role-specific prompts, and post-session analysis that tracks progress over time.
features: Real-time voice interview via VAPI WebRTC with live transcript and mid-interview AI feedback
50+ roles across 6 industries with 7-level adaptive difficulty and AI-generated topic selection
In-session tool panels: code editor, markdown notebook, whiteboard (tldraw), and spreadsheet — all switchable without interrupting the call
Credit-based billing via Paddle with subscription renewal, one-time packs, and FIFO credit consumption
role: Solo full-stack developer — architecture, backend, frontend, design, DevOps
stackSummary: Next.js 16 + React 19 with raw PostgreSQL (Neon), VAPI voice AI, multi-provider LLM (DeepSeek/OpenAI/Gemini) via Vercel AI SDK, Paddle billing, and Upstash Redis rate limiting.
whatILearned: Integrating a real-time voice AI SDK (VAPI) into a React app — managing call lifecycle, state machines, and audio sessions with custom hooks.
Building a multi-provider LLM pipeline (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Gemini) using Vercel AI SDK for dynamic system prompt generation.
Designing a credit-based billing system with Paddle (webhooks, subscription renewal, one-time packs) and FIFO credit consumption logic.
Writing a secure webhook layer: Svix signatures for Clerk, JWT nonce verification for VAPI, Paddle SDK for billing events.
Architecting complex React hook compositions — splitting a VAPI session into 8+ focused hooks (call state, lifecycle, message pipeline, focus mode, heartbeat, live feedback).
Lazy-loading a heavy landing page (12+ sections) while preserving Core Web Vitals with Next.js dynamic imports.
Implementing serverless-safe rate limiting with Upstash Redis across API routes.
Parsing user-uploaded CVs (PDF) server-side for AI context injection.
Maintaining a raw SQL codebase without an ORM at meaningful scale.

particularAspects.title: Role library
particularAspects.content: 50+ interview roles across 6 industries (Tech, Finance, Design, Business, Health, Education) — each with a carefully crafted AI prompt.

particularAspects.title: Dual session modes
particularAspects.content: Dual session modes: live voice interview (VAPI WebRTC) and written interview — same agent, different transport.

particularAspects.title: Session workspace
particularAspects.content: Session UI includes a live transcript panel, code editor, markdown notebook, whiteboard (tldraw), and spreadsheet panel — all switchable mid-call without interrupting audio.

particularAspects.title: Live feedback
particularAspects.content: Live feedback system that fires a parallel LLM request during the interview without pausing the VAPI audio stream, then injects the result at the right transcript position.

designFocus: Dark-first design with emerald green accent (#10b981) on near-black backgrounds (#07070a, #0f0f13).
Framer Motion fadeUp stagger animations on all landing sections with blur-in effect.
Syne font for display headlines, Plus Jakarta Sans for body — tight negative letter-spacing on hero text.
Agents slider with per-agent dynamic color via CSS --agent-color variable.
Dot-grid and bg-grid decorative backgrounds scoped to specific sections.
Marquee sections with edge-fade masks and pause-on-hover.
Equalizer waveform pixel animation (PixelMic) as a mic activity indicator.
Shader-animated aurora backgrounds for the pricing section.
Consistent card pattern: #0f0f13 bg, gradient border, glow box-shadow on hover.
Both light and dark theme via next-themes + CSS variable switching.
developmentFocus: Raw SQL only — no ORM, all queries via @neondatabase/serverless tagged template literals.
Strict TypeScript throughout — shared types in types/index.d.ts, Zod validation at all API boundaries.
Custom multi-hook architecture for VAPI session: useCallState, useCallLifecycle, useMessagePipeline, useFocusMode, useVoiceSessionHeartbeat, useLiveFeedback.
WebRTC voice connectors abstracted into pluggable modules (VAPI, OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live).
Webhook security: Svix for Clerk, JWT nonce pattern for VAPI, Paddle SDK for billing.
Vitest test suite with vi.mock patterns for SQL, Clerk auth, and NextResponse.
Upstash Redis rate limiting on sensitive API routes.
Sentry for both server and client error tracking.
CV parsing pipeline: PDF upload → Vercel Blob → pdfjs-dist extraction → AI context injection.
Lazy-loaded landing page with next/dynamic for all below-fold sections.
interactionDetails: User picks a role, difficulty (1–7), duration, language, and live feedback toggle before starting.
Voice session starts via VAPI WebRTC; user speaks, agent responds in real time.
During the call, the agent can push code challenges live to the notebook panel.
Post-call: AI-generated structured feedback with score, strengths, areas to improve, and question breakdown.
Written mode: typed Q&A with the same underlying AI agent, no voice.
Credit meter visible during session; banner shown when credits expire mid-call.
Session sidebar shows real-time transcript, tool panels, and session controls.
technicalHighlights: VAPI call lifecycle decomposed into 8+ composable React hooks — not a monolith.
JWT nonce system for VAPI webhook replay-attack prevention.
Multi-LLM fallback chain: DeepSeek primary, OpenAI/Gemini as alternatives via Vercel AI SDK.
Interview heartbeat API keeps session alive and tracks real-time credit consumption server-side.
Structured feedback stored in PostgreSQL and surfaced in a progressive dashboard with historical tracking.
Proctor mode as a separate client route for supervised interview sessions.
Chrome extension auth flow with a dedicated SSO callback and extension-specific redirect.
portfolioValue: Demonstrates end-to-end product engineering at SaaS scale: real-time voice AI integration, multi-provider LLM orchestration, secure billing webhooks, complex React hook architecture, and a polished animated landing page — all solo-built.

suggestedCaseStudyText.overview: InterSpeak is an AI voice interview coach that lets users practice job interviews across 50+ roles and 6 industries. Users select a role and difficulty, then speak directly with an AI interviewer in real time via WebRTC. The platform supports dual session modes (voice and written), live mid-interview feedback, and structured post-session analysis — all gated behind a credit-based subscription.
suggestedCaseStudyText.learnings: The hardest part was managing VAPI's call lifecycle alongside React's rendering model without creating a monolithic component. I decomposed the session into 8+ focused hooks (call state, lifecycle, message pipeline, focus mode, heartbeat, live feedback) that compose cleanly. I also learned how to build a secure webhook layer for three different providers simultaneously — Svix for Clerk, a JWT nonce system for VAPI, and the Paddle SDK for billing events — each with different trust models.
suggestedCaseStudyText.particularAspects: The session UI is unusually rich for a voice app: a live transcript, a code editor with challenge injection mid-call, a markdown notebook, a whiteboard via tldraw, and a spreadsheet panel — all switchable without interrupting the call. The live feedback system fires a parallel LLM request during the interview without pausing the VAPI audio stream, then injects the result into the transcript at the right position.
suggestedCaseStudyText.outcome: A production-ready SaaS with a full billing stack, admin tooling, Chrome extension integration, and a Vitest test suite. The landing page achieves fast initial paint via aggressive lazy-loading of below-fold sections, while still delivering heavy visual polish (shader backgrounds, Framer Motion stagger animations, waveform equalizer).

title: Swaggerz
shortDescription: Landing page for an imaginary streetwear brand, with custom WebGL shaders, scroll-driven animations, and a semantic design system built from scratch.
fullDescription: Swaggerz is a landing page for an imaginary streetwear brand, built as a technical exercise to explore integrating custom WebGL shaders into a Next.js 15 application. The goal was to bring interactive generative graphics into the React DOM without compromising performance.
problem: Integrating real-time WebGL graphics into a React app creates performance pitfalls: multiple renderer contexts, GPU overhead, and lifecycle mismatches. Swaggerz explores how to solve these problems with a Singleton renderer, visibility-based throttling, and careful resource cleanup.
features: ShaderText hero title rendered via GLSL fragment shader applied as an SVG pattern fill
Liquid video shader that reacts to cursor position with simplex noise and UV distortion
SharedRendererManager singleton sharing one WebGLRenderer across all shader components
Magic link + Google OAuth via Better Auth with Drizzle ORM sessions
stackSummary: Next.js 15 with App Router and Turbopack, Three.js for WebGL shaders, Framer Motion for UI animations, Lenis for smooth scroll. Backend with Drizzle ORM on PostgreSQL Neon and magic-link auth via Better Auth.
whatILearned: Writing GLSL fragment shaders for complex visual effects: simplex noise, UV distortion, liquid effect on video and images.
Singleton pattern to share a single WebGLRenderer across multiple React components, avoiding multiple WebGL contexts and reducing GPU overhead.
Using a shader as an SVG fill pattern: render on a hidden canvas and use the dataUrl in an SVG <pattern> to apply animated shaders to scalable text.
Managing the WebGL lifecycle in React with correct cleanup (dispose of geometry, material, texture, renderer) and IntersectionObserver to pause rendering outside the viewport.
Structuring a semantic design system with Tailwind v4 (@theme): functional token names instead of numbers (text-light-secondary, bg-dark-element, p-xl).
Loading optimization: lazy loading with next/dynamic for below-the-fold sections, static SSR hero image + progressive client-side slideshow, transferToImageBitmap for faster canvas copies.
Integrating Better Auth with magic link and Google OAuth, managing CORS across environments (Codespaces, localhost).

particularAspects.title: Hero shaders
particularAspects.content: ShaderText: the 'SwaggerZ' hero title is rendered with an animated GLSL fragment shader (red-orange-yellow waves) applied as an SVG pattern, reusing geometry and material via a Singleton (ShaderTextRenderer) — an unusual approach compared to direct canvas solutions.

particularAspects.title: Video shader
particularAspects.content: LiquidVideoShader: a looping video in the hero is processed in real time by a Three.js fragment shader that reacts to the cursor with simplex noise and UV distortion, with smooth fade-in/out via JS-side lerp.

particularAspects.title: Shared renderer
particularAspects.content: SharedRendererManager: a singleton manages a single WebGLRenderer for all ShaderText components on the page, with priority queues, FPS throttling per task, and lazy visibility to avoid wasting GPU.

particularAspects.title: Wave cards
particularAspects.content: WaveImageShader: category cards use a wave shader with configurable parameters (amplitude, waveSpeed) and resize handling via ResizeObserver with dynamic mesh scale recalculation.

designFocus: Dark premium aesthetic with zinc-950/black base palette and orange-500 as brand accent.
Brand signature gradient: red → orange → yellow used on the logo, hero title, and shader text.
Display typography with a custom decorative font (Pastor of Muppets) completed by the animated shader.
Animated scroll indicator with Framer Motion that disappears after the first scroll.
Themed loader (SwagLoader) with custom SVG spinner and rotating Italian status messages.
Semantic design system with functional tokens documented in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md.
developmentFocus: WebGL/Three.js without @react-three/fiber for fine-grained renderer lifecycle control.
Singleton pattern for renderer sharing across React instances (SharedRendererManager, ShaderTextRenderer).
Aggressive lazy loading: next/dynamic for every below-the-fold section, AVIF images with SSR priority.
IntersectionObserver to pause rendering and video when off-screen.
Full auth: magic link + Google OAuth + sessions with Drizzle ORM.
Database seeding with tsx scripts and Drizzle Studio for inspection.
interactionDetails: Hover on the hero video: cursor generates liquid waves in the shader (simplex noise + mouse attraction, with fade-out after 150ms of inactivity).
Hover on category cards: mouse position updates the uMouse uniform in the wave shader.
Global smooth scroll via Lenis with custom exponential easing.
Entrance animations with Framer Motion (opacity + translateY) on hero content with sequential delays.
Hero image slideshow with Embla Carousel loaded progressively after the first render.
CTA button with hover animation on the arrow icon (translate + scale).
technicalHighlights: Three distinct custom GLSL fragment shaders: animated display text (cycling RGB waves), liquid distortion on video (cursor-reactive simplex noise), wave effect on static images — each with a different React lifecycle.
SharedRenderer singleton with task queue, FPS throttling per task, lazy visibility, and renderer pre-warm to eliminate first-frame stutter.
Shader text via SVG pattern: hidden canvas → dataUrl → <image> in SVG <pattern> → <text> fill — a technique that enables any canvas/WebGL effect as a scalable text fill.
transferToImageBitmap as a canvas-to-canvas blit optimization (~50% faster than drawImage), with feature detection and fallback.
Better Auth with magic link: 10-minute token expiry, 7-day sessions, CORS configured for GitHub Codespaces wildcard patterns.
portfolioValue: Demonstrates the ability to integrate generative WebGL graphics into a production-grade Next.js application, with attention to performance (renderer sharing, lazy loading, visibility-based throttling) and a consistent design system. The project goes beyond using libraries: GLSL shaders are written from scratch and the architectural patterns (Singleton, task queue) are custom solutions to real React rendering problems.

suggestedCaseStudyText.overview: Swaggerz is a landing page for an imaginary streetwear brand, built as a technical exercise to explore integrating custom WebGL shaders into a Next.js 15 application. The goal was to bring interactive generative graphics into the React DOM without compromising performance.
suggestedCaseStudyText.learnings: The most interesting challenge was sharing a WebGLRenderer across multiple React components without creating multiple contexts. The solution is a Singleton (SharedRendererManager) with a task queue, priorities, and per-task FPS throttling — an architecture that then made it possible to animate the hero title via shader with no additional overhead. I also discovered the technique of using a hidden WebGL canvas as the source for an SVG pattern, which enables any shader to be applied as a scalable text fill.
suggestedCaseStudyText.particularAspects: Three distinct shaders for three contexts: one for display text (cycling RGB waves), one for the hero video (cursor-reactive liquid distortion via simplex noise), one for category cards (animatable wave with configurable parameters). Each shader has a different React lifecycle and required different solutions for cleanup, resize, and synchronization with the shared renderer.
suggestedCaseStudyText.outcome: The result is a page with non-trivial visual effects that stays performant through lazy rendering (IntersectionObserver pauses shaders off-screen), progressive section loading, and a documented, consistent design system. An exercise that solidified understanding of WebGL, GLSL, and the patterns for managing GPU resources in React applications.

SplitText for char-by-char and word-by-word animations with stagger.

title: Apple MacBook Pro — Landing Page Clone
shortDescription: Interactive replica of the Apple MacBook Pro landing page, with navigable 3D models, scroll-driven animations, and a design system faithful to the original.
fullDescription: A clone of Apple's MacBook Pro landing page built as a technical and visual exercise. The project features a fully interactive 3D viewer with color and size selection, a Features section with videos projected onto the MacBook screen in real time synchronized with scroll, a Performance section with geometrically positioned photo cards that fan out on scroll, and a Showcase section with a cinematic SVG mask reveal. Every section is animated via GSAP ScrollTrigger with pinned timelines, scrub, and multi-step sequences.
problem: Replicating a reference design like Apple's requires solving non-trivial problems at the intersection of WebGL rendering, DOM animation, and performance: keeping the 3D rotation loop synchronized with GSAP's scroll progress, applying a live VideoTexture to a 3D mesh, and computing dynamic card positions without hardcoding layout values.
features: VideoTexture projected live onto the MacBook 3D screen — switches video per feature on scroll via GSAP ScrollTrigger
360° scroll-driven 3D rotation: scrollProgress passed from ScrollTrigger to R3F useFrame keeps DOM and WebGL in sync
Performance section: 7 photo cards positioned geometrically in vw/vh units fan out from a central point with per-card rotations on scroll
Color picker applies a new Three.js Color to model materials in real time, excluding a curated noChangeParts list

whatILearned: Integrating .glb 3D models in React via React Three Fiber and gltfjsx to generate typed components from GLTF files.
Applying Three.js VideoTexture to project live video onto the MacBook screen, synchronized with scroll.
Orchestrating GSAP ScrollTrigger for pin, scrub, and multi-step timelines with precise progress control.
Coordinating scroll progress and 3D rotation via R3F's useFrame, bridging the DOM world and the WebGL loop.
Setting up realistic studio lighting in Three.js for PBR materials and photorealistic rendering.
Managing global state shared between Three.js and DOM components via Zustand.
Geometrically computing card positions in the Performance section with dynamic vw/vh offsets per breakpoint.
Animating SVG masks with GSAP matrix transforms (scale 80x → 1.1) for a cinematic Apple-style logo reveal.

Animated card stacking with rotations and scale in the Performance section on scroll.

DOM ↔ WebGL synchronization via shared React state (scrollProgress) between ScrollTrigger and useFrame.
SVG mask with GSAP matrix transformation from scale 80 for a cinematic zoom-out effect.

portfolioValue: Demonstrates simultaneous mastery of advanced web animation (GSAP), in-browser 3D rendering (Three.js/R3F), and attention to visual detail in replicating a reference design like Apple's. The standout is the synchronization between the DOM world and the WebGL loop.

suggestedCaseStudyText.overview: Clone of the Apple MacBook Pro landing page, built to explore the integration between 3D rendering, scroll-driven animations, and high-quality design systems. The project includes an interactive 3D viewer with color and size selection, a Features section with videos projected onto the model screen, and multiple sections with animations orchestrated via GSAP ScrollTrigger.
suggestedCaseStudyText.learnings: The project required solving a non-trivial problem: synchronizing the WebGL rendering loop (R3F's useFrame) with the DOM animation system (GSAP ScrollTrigger). The solution is to pass scrollProgress as React state, letting useFrame update the model rotation every frame without direct coupling. Equally interesting was managing live VideoTexture on a 3D mesh, which requires attention to colorSpace, needsUpdate, and the lifecycle of manually created video elements.
suggestedCaseStudyText.particularAspects: The most distinctive aspect is the Features section: a 3D MacBook locked to the center of the screen rotates 360° while scrolling, and the model screen plays a different video for each of the five features. Everything is orchestrated by a single GSAP timeline with pin, without needing to coordinate multiple separate ScrollTriggers. The Performance section uses a geometric approach to position 7 photo cards that fan out from a central point toward positions computed in vw/vh.
suggestedCaseStudyText.outcome: The result is a single-page application that faithfully replicates the visual experience of the Apple site, working on mobile, tablet, and desktop. It is a concrete example of how Three.js, GSAP, and React can coexist in a complex project while maintaining acceptable performance through preloading, model optimization, and correct animation cleanup.

title: Portfolio 2024
shortDescription: Interactive single-page portfolio with 3D WebGL globe, cursor-tracking blob, canvas particle effects, and Framer Motion micro-animations.
fullDescription: A personal developer portfolio built with Next.js 14 as a fully client-rendered single-page app. It presents the developer's identity, projects, soft skills, and educational background through a series of heavily animated sections — each with distinct motion and WebGL effects. The stack combines React Three Fiber for 3D rendering, Framer Motion for declarative animation, and custom canvas shaders for interactive visual effects.
problem: How do you present a developer who is self-taught and transitioning from a humanities background in a way that stands out? The creative challenge was to build something visually ambitious enough to prove frontend competence — not just to list skills, but to demonstrate them through the site itself.
features: Hero with pointer-tracking glow blob that fades out as user scrolls past the section, managed via IntersectionObserver to avoid idle event listeners
BentoGrid layout (6-cell asymmetric grid) embedding a live interactive 3D globe rendered with Three.js and three-globe
Recent Projects section using a custom 3D Pin hover card that lifts and tilts on interaction
Motivation section with letter-level proximity animation: hovering a skill word triggers per-character vertical bounce and color blending toward purple based on distance from cursor
Approach section with three cards that reveal a WebGL CanvasRevealEffect (animated dot grid) on hover using AnimatePresence
Studies/Experience section with animated moving-border cards powered by a custom Framer Motion SVG path border animation
stackSummary: Next.js 14 provides the App Router shell and static export. All sections are client components ('use client') because they rely on browser APIs and animation hooks. Tailwind CSS handles layout and utility styling; Framer Motion drives entrance animations, hover states, and the AnimatePresence-guarded reveal effects. Three.js is brought in twice — once via @react-three/fiber for the 3D globe in the BentoGrid, and once as three-globe for the globe geometry itself. Sentry is wired in at the Next.js instrumentation layer for production error and session replay monitoring.
whatILearned: Integrating Three.js and React Three Fiber inside Next.js App Router, including the 'use client' boundary requirements for WebGL canvases
Performance-conscious event listener management: attaching/removing pointermove and scroll listeners based on IntersectionObserver state to avoid dead listeners when components are off-screen
Canvas-based particle/dot reveal effects — implementing a shader-driven dot grid that animates in on hover
Per-character animation with proximity-based math: calculating letter-level color blending and Y offset as a function of distance from the hovered character index
Composing a local design system in components/ui/ — reusable primitives (MagicButton, MovingBorder, Spotlight, BentoGrid) that keep section components thin
Sentry integration in Next.js including session replay for capturing real user interactions in production

particularAspects.title: The CanvasRevealEffect uses a WebGL
particularAspects.content: The CanvasRevealEffect uses a WebGL dot-matrix shader that animates radially from the cursor on hover — implemented from scratch rather than using a library

particularAspects.title: The cursor blob in the
particularAspects.content: The cursor blob in the Hero does not use CSS cursor tricks: it is an absolutely-positioned div repositioned on every pointermove event, with opacity and scale controlled by a separate scroll-position check

particularAspects.title: The letter-wave animation in the
particularAspects.content: The letter-wave animation in the Motivation section computes a custom color interpolation between white and purple (rgb 203,172,249) with a max-distance falloff of 3 characters, giving a smooth ripple that is purely mathematical with no CSS keyframes

particularAspects.title: three-globe is used inside a
particularAspects.content: three-globe is used inside a @react-three/fiber Canvas, requiring careful integration of the imperative Three.js object with React's declarative render cycle

designFocus: Dark-first design with a consistent near-black background (rgb 4,7,29 → 12,14,35 gradient) and a single purple accent color (#CBACF9) used across all interactive highlights
BentoGrid creates visual hierarchy through asymmetric spanning cells — the globe card spans the full left column height, anchoring the layout
Spotlight effects in the Hero cast two overlapping colored light cones at the top of the viewport, giving a cinematic stage-light feel before the user reads any text
All section cards use rounded-3xl corners and a subtle border (border-white/[0.2]) for a frosted-glass aesthetic consistent with the dark background
Typography intentionally minimal — section headings use a single large weight change with a purple word highlight, avoiding decorative fonts
developmentFocus: All reusable interactive primitives live in components/ui/ — FloatingNavbar, BentoGrid, 3d-pin, CanvasRevealEffect, MovingBorder, Spotlight, TextGenerateEffect, InfiniteMovingCards — keeping section components purely compositional
Data is centralized in a single data/index.js file exporting navItems, gridItems, projects, motivation, softSkill, workExperience, and socialMedia — zero props drilling, all sections import directly
next-themes wraps the app for dark mode support at the provider level, allowing future light-mode styling without structural changes
Sentry is integrated at the Next.js instrumentation level (not just client-side), meaning server-side errors and session replays are both captured
tailwind-merge and clsx are used together for conditional className composition, avoiding class conflicts in shared utility components
interactionDetails: Cursor blob in Hero: an absolutely-positioned radial gradient div tracks pointer coordinates in real time via pointermove; when the cursor crosses into the bottom padding zone it fades to opacity 0 and scale 0.5 with a 0.4s ease transition

Approach cards: hovering triggers AnimatePresence to mount the CanvasRevealEffect, which fires a WebGL shader animation — each of the three cards has a different color palette (green, pink, yellow) for the dot reveal

Motivation skill tiles: each character in the label is an individual motion.span; hovering the tile triggers a wave of Y-displacement (max -15px at center, tapering to 0 at ±3 chars) and a white-to-purple color blend, all spring-animated (stiffness 300, damping 20)
FloatingNavbar appears/disappears based on scroll direction — it floats over content and hides when scrolling down fast, reducing visual noise during reading
technicalHighlights: IntersectionObserver guards the Hero's pointermove/scroll listeners — they are only registered when the Hero is at least 50% visible, preventing silent event listeners from running on every frame while the user is on a different section

The CanvasRevealEffect is a self-contained WebGL component using a raw canvas element and requestAnimationFrame, not wrapped in @react-three/fiber — it demonstrates direct WebGL usage alongside the Three.js fiber usage elsewhere in the same project

The 3D Pin card uses CSS perspective and CSS custom properties to create a true 3D tilt perspective shift on the container, not Framer Motion — the pin SVG animates separately via a CSS keyframe drop-shadow pulse

Sentry @sentry/replay is included alongside the standard SDK, meaning real user session videos are captured in production — a non-trivial addition to a personal portfolio that shows awareness of production observability
lodash.throttle is imported selectively (lodash.throttle, not full lodash) indicating deliberate bundle-size awareness
portfolioValue: This project demonstrates that visual ambition and technical precision can coexist: every animation in the site is backed by a concrete technical decision — IntersectionObserver lifecycle management, per-character spring physics, WebGL canvas shaders. For a developer whose background is non-traditional (humanities degree, self-taught), the site itself acts as proof-of-work, showing command of Three.js, Framer Motion, and Next.js App Router in a single coherent product. The inclusion of Sentry with session replay on a personal portfolio signals production-mindedness beyond what the project strictly requires.

suggestedCaseStudyText.overview: This personal portfolio is a Next.js 14 single-page app built in 2024 to present my frontend capabilities to potential clients and collaborators. It was designed to demonstrate, not just describe, technical skill — every section uses a distinct interaction or rendering technique rather than static content.
suggestedCaseStudyText.learnings: The hardest parts were the WebGL integrations: wiring three-globe inside a React Three Fiber canvas, and building the CanvasRevealEffect dot-grid shader from scratch. I also had to solve a subtle performance bug where pointermove listeners in the Hero continued running off-screen — fixed by gating them behind an IntersectionObserver so they only attach when the section is visible.
suggestedCaseStudyText.particularAspects: The Motivation section's letter-wave is the interaction I'm most proud of: each character is an individual motion.span, and hovering triggers a spring-physics bounce and a proximity-based color blend computed with pure arithmetic — no CSS keyframes. The per-character distance falloff gives a fluid ripple that feels physical rather than scripted.
suggestedCaseStudyText.outcome: The result is a production-deployed portfolio with Sentry monitoring and session replay, demonstrating not just UI aesthetics but also observability awareness. It serves as a live showcase of React animation patterns, Three.js integration, and component architecture that I reference in every frontend conversation.

title: Portfolio 2026
shortDescription: Personal portfolio with custom GLSL shaders, a CSS 3D dome gallery, scroll-driven animations, ambient music player, and full EN/IT localisation — built as a complete design and engineering exercise.
fullDescription: This portfolio is built as a complete product, not just a showcase page. Every section is a distinct visual and technical experiment: a persistent WebGL shader background that survives client-side navigation, a 3D dome gallery with gesture-controlled rotation, a scroll-pinned SVG mask reveal, per-section shader color variants, and an ambient music player backed by a singleton Audio instance. The site is fully bilingual (EN/IT) via next-intl and includes a contact form with Cloudflare Turnstile anti-bot protection and Resend email delivery.
problem: A personal portfolio needs to communicate both design sensibility and technical depth without becoming a boilerplate Next.js template. The challenge was making every section feel unique while keeping the codebase clean and the performance solid.
features: PersistentShaderLayer: a globally mounted WebGL canvas repositioned via getBoundingClientRect — survives Next.js client-side navigation
DomeGallery: CSS 3D dome with gesture rotation (@use-gesture), seeded shuffle (FNV-1a + Mulberry32) and 35-segment grid
ComparisonSection: GSAP ScrollTrigger pinned SVG spark mask scaling from fullscreen to reveal the AI vs Developer split
Full EN/IT localisation via next-intl with server-side translations and locale-based routing
stackSummary: Next.js 16 App Router with server components, @react-three/fiber for WebGL shaders, Framer Motion and GSAP for scroll animations, Lenis for smooth scroll, next-intl for i18n, Resend + @vercel/postgres for contact form backend.
whatILearned: How to keep a WebGL canvas alive across Next.js route changes: mount it globally, track the hero section's bounding rect on each scroll frame, and toggle rendering only when the section is in view.
Writing configurable GLSL fragment shaders with value noise, rotation matrices, and a smoothstep diagonal cut — parameterised per section via a ShaderVariant interface.

Building a CSS 3D dome without WebGL: pure perspective/rotateX/rotateY transforms on absolutely positioned tiles, with a seeded PRNG (FNV-1a hash + Mulberry32) for reproducible shuffle across server and client renders.
Singleton HTMLAudioElement kept outside React state so playback survives hydration, route transitions, and Strict Mode double-mounting.

Coordinating GSAP ScrollTrigger pin + SVG mask scale in a single timeline, computing the initial scale from the spark bounding box relative to the viewport so it fills the screen correctly on any window size.
Setting up next-intl with App Router: locale-based segments, server-side getTranslations, and a LanguageSwitcher that preserves the current pathname.

particularAspects.title: Persistent canvas
particularAspects.content: PersistentShaderLayer mounts a fixed canvas once in the root layout and dynamically repositions it over the hero section by reading getBoundingClientRect on each scroll event — the WebGL context is never destroyed on navigation.

particularAspects.title: Water shader
particularAspects.content: WaterPlaneShader is a custom GLSL fragment shader with a value-noise function, a Rot(a) rotation matrix, a smoothstep diagonal cut, and a grain hash overlay — every parameter (colorA, colorB, fillTint, frequency, amplitude, speed) is exposed as a uniform, allowing each ABCSection panel to have its own distinct visual identity.

particularAspects.title: Dome gallery
particularAspects.content: DomeGallery places image tiles on a CSS 3D cylinder (35 segments × 5–6 rows) with per-tile base rotation calculated from its grid position. A seeded PRNG (FNV-1a over the image URL/alt set) produces a reproducible shuffle so the layout is consistent between SSR and hydration.

particularAspects.title: Comparison timeline
particularAspects.content: ComparisonSection uses a GSAP timeline with two fromTo tweens: first opacity 0→1 at full scale, then scale down to 1 — computed at runtime from the SVG spark bounding box and viewport size so the effect fills the screen on any device.

designFocus: Black base palette with cyan and white accents; shader backgrounds as the primary design element rather than decorative add-ons.
ABCSection: three scroll-pinned panels (A/B/C skill categories), each with a unique GLSL shader color variant (green→teal, cyan→blue, magenta→pink).
ComparisonSection: full-bleed SVG spark mask reveal — the bolt shape grows from a single point to cover the entire viewport on scroll.
FloatingNav: transitions from inline to a pill-shaped floating bar after first scroll, hides on scroll-down and reappears on scroll-up.
MusicPlayer: ambient track selector in the nav with AnimatePresence crossfade on track title change.
developmentFocus: App Router with Server Components by default; Client Components only where interaction, animation, or browser APIs are needed.
next-intl with locale segment routing: /en/* and /it/*, server-side translations loaded per page, root redirect from / to /en.
Contact form: Cloudflare Turnstile server-side validation → Resend transactional email → @vercel/postgres message persistence.
WaterPlaneShader abstraction: ShaderVariant interface decouples visual parameters from shader code, allowing any component to pass a variant without touching GLSL.
DomeGallery as a self-contained JSX component with no external 3D library — all 3D achieved with CSS transforms and perspective.
interactionDetails: Drag on DomeGallery rotates the dome horizontally with momentum and a vertical tilt limit of ±5°; tile click expands the selected card in place.
ABCSection scroll progress (Framer Motion useScroll) drives panel transitions between A, B, and C — with a Swiper carousel fallback on mobile.
ComparisonSection is pinned for 150% scroll distance; the GSAP timeline ties SVG scale directly to scroll progress.
Lenis smooth scroll applied globally; ScrollBanner uses a CSS sticky reveal triggered by scroll position.
FloatingNav hides on downward scroll (threshold: 100px) and reappears instantly on upward scroll.
technicalHighlights: Persistent WebGL context via a globally mounted canvas that reads hero bounding rect on scroll — eliminates teardown/setup cost when navigating between pages.
Custom GLSL value-noise function with a Rot(a) matrix and a smoothstep diagonal cut, all exposed as configurable uniforms — no shader library dependency.
CSS 3D dome without WebGL: cylinder geometry computed purely from CSS perspective and rotateX/Y transforms on a grid of absolutely positioned tiles.
FNV-1a hash over image URLs/alts → Mulberry32 PRNG → Fisher-Yates shuffle ensures the same tile order on every server and client render, preventing hydration mismatch.

GSAP ScrollTrigger scale computed at runtime: spark half-width/height in SVG units multiplied by the cover-scale factor, then a 1.4× safety margin — guarantees the mask fills the screen at every viewport size.
portfolioValue: Demonstrates the ability to design and engineer a complete web product from scratch with independent choices at every layer: custom GLSL shaders without a shader library, CSS 3D without Three.js where appropriate, scroll animations with both Framer Motion and GSAP, a persistent rendering architecture that survives navigation, and production-grade backend features (i18n, contact form, anti-bot, email). The result shows both visual design sensibility and systems-level thinking.

suggestedCaseStudyText.overview: This portfolio is built as a complete product, not a static showcase. Every section is a self-contained visual and technical exercise: a persistent WebGL shader background that survives client-side navigation, a CSS 3D dome gallery with gesture rotation, a GSAP scroll-pinned SVG mask reveal, per-section shader color variants, and an ambient music player backed by a singleton Audio instance. The site is fully bilingual (EN/IT) via next-intl and includes a contact form with Cloudflare Turnstile and Resend email delivery.
suggestedCaseStudyText.learnings: The most interesting architectural challenge was keeping a WebGL canvas alive across route transitions in Next.js. The solution — a globally mounted canvas that repositions itself over the hero section by reading getBoundingClientRect on scroll — means the GPU context is never destroyed and the first frame on re-visit is instant. A similar singleton pattern was applied to the audio player: one HTMLAudioElement created outside React, shared via context, surviving Strict Mode double-mounting and hot-reloads. Writing the WaterPlaneShader also clarified how to structure configurable GLSL: expose every visual parameter as a uniform, define a TypeScript interface for the variant, and keep the GLSL itself parameter-agnostic.
suggestedCaseStudyText.particularAspects: DomeGallery is the most unusual component: a CSS 3D cylinder made entirely of absolutely positioned tiles with rotateX/Y transforms — no Three.js or WebGL. A seeded PRNG (FNV-1a hash + Mulberry32) ensures the shuffle is reproducible between SSR and hydration, preventing any layout shift. The ComparisonSection SVG mask effect computes the initial scale at runtime from the spark bounding box and viewport dimensions, so the bolt always fills the screen exactly before animating down to 1× via GSAP ScrollTrigger.
suggestedCaseStudyText.outcome: A deployed personal site that serves as both a portfolio and a live demonstration of frontend engineering choices: custom shaders, CSS 3D, scroll orchestration, i18n, and a backend contact pipeline — all integrated into a single Next.js 16 App Router codebase.

title: Dev Overflow
shortDescription: A full-stack Stack Overflow clone with questions, answers, voting, tags, collections, and AI-assisted answer generation via OpenAI GPT.
fullDescription: Dev Overflow is a functional clone of Stack Overflow built as a full-stack technical exercise. It implements the core platform features — questions, answers, votes, tags, profiles, collections — using the modern Next.js 16 App Router stack with MongoDB, and adds an original feature: AI-assisted answer generation via OpenAI GPT.
problem: Building a real-world Q&A platform requires solving non-trivial problems at every layer: multi-provider auth with DB persistence, rich text editing with syntax highlighting, vote deduplication, server-side search and pagination, and AI integration with per-user rate limiting.
features: AI answer generation (HTML-native, Tiptap-compatible) with per-user rate limiting and atomic rollback
NextAuth v5 with GitHub, Google OAuth and credentials — user/account created atomically via Mongoose transactions
Tiptap v3 rich text editor with code blocks, syntax highlighting, and sanitized HTML preview
Votes, bookmarks, tags, collections, profiles, and server-side search with URL state
stackSummary: Next.js 16 App Router with Server Actions for all mutations, MongoDB via Mongoose, NextAuth v5, Tiptap for rich text editing, OpenAI GPT via Vercel AI SDK, Tailwind v4 with Radix UI and Shadcn.
whatILearned: Implementing NextAuth v5 with OAuth (GitHub, Google) and credentials providers, persisting user/account in MongoDB via Mongoose transactions inside JWT callbacks.
Structuring typed Server Actions with a uniform response pattern (ActionResponse) for centralized error handling without scattered try/catch on the client.
Integrating Tiptap as a rich text editor with custom extensions (code block with lowlight, inline syntax highlighting), safe HTML serialization via sanitize-html, and a separate preview component.
Building an AI API protected by per-user rate limiting: a 3-generation limit stored on MongoDB with atomic rollback on OpenAI error.
Managing URL state for filters, search, and pagination with query-string, keeping navigation stale-free in Next.js App Router.
Using Suspense boundaries to defer heavy content (votes, bookmark state) without blocking page render.
Implementing an upvote/downvote system on questions and answers with DB-level deduplication.

particularAspects.title: OAuth flow
particularAspects.content: The OAuth flow is handled entirely in NextAuth's signIn callback with a Mongoose transaction: if the account already exists it's a no-op; otherwise it creates user + account atomically, including unique username generation via slug + progressive suffix.

particularAspects.title: HTML generation
particularAspects.content: AI generation responds in native HTML (not Markdown) directly compatible with Tiptap — the system prompt instructs GPT to use only editor-supported tags and to preserve the user's existing draft.

particularAspects.title: Dual submit states
particularAspects.content: AnswerForm uses useTransition for manual submit and a separate flag for AI submit, managing two independent loading states in the same UI.

particularAspects.title: AI rate limiting
particularAspects.content: AI rate limiting is implemented with a findOneAndUpdate conditional query on aiAnswerGenerations — no explicit locks, leveraging MongoDB atomicity.

designFocus: Three-column layout: left sidebar (navigation), center (content), right sidebar (top tags/users) — faithful to the Stack Overflow layout.
Dark/light mode with next-themes and conditional Tailwind classes (text-dark100_light900 pattern).
Radix UI components for native accessibility (dialog, dropdown, select, tabs, toast).
Tailwind Typography plugin for rich text content rendering in question/answer previews.
developmentFocus: App Router with Server Components by default, Client Components only where interaction is needed.
Server Actions for all mutations: questions, answers, votes, collections, profile.
Zod schema validation both client-side (react-hook-form) and server-side (in actions and the AI API route).
Structured logging with Pino for debugging DB and API operations.
ESLint config with import, prettier, and simple-import-sort plugins for codebase consistency.
Turbopack enabled in dev for faster builds.
interactionDetails: Local search with debounce hooked to URL params — no extra fetches, the page updates server-side.
Category filters (Newest, Recommended, Frequent, Unanswered) managed via searchParams.
Server-side pagination with isNext cursor.
Tiptap editor with contextual toolbar, code blocks with syntax highlight, and dynamic placeholder.
'Generate AI Answer' button that calls the API, shows a dedicated spinner, and injects the result directly into the editor without overwriting the draft.
Toast notifications for submit feedback, errors, and rate limit reached.
Save/unsave questions with optimistic update via Server Action.
Votes with server-loaded initial state updated client-side.
technicalHighlights: NextAuth v5 with custom JWT callback that resolves the MongoDB user ID from the providerAccountId — decoupling OAuth identity from application identity.
Mongoose transactions in OAuth flows to guarantee user/account consistency under race conditions.
AI API route with counter rollback on provider error (try/catch with compensating decrement).
Dynamic generateMetadata for SEO on every question detail page with Open Graph.
Clear separation between Preview (sanitized HTML rendering) and Editor (interactive Tiptap) as distinct components.
Username generation with slugify + DB uniqueness loop — robust on edge cases like special-character names or duplicate users.
portfolioValue: Demonstrates mastery of the modern Next.js App Router stack with real-world patterns: complex multi-provider auth, AI integration with guardrails, advanced rich text editing, and a server-action-first architecture. The implementation choices (Mongoose transactions in OAuth, atomic rate limiting, AI rollback) show independent technical reasoning beyond tutorial-level work.

suggestedCaseStudyText.overview: Dev Overflow is a functional clone of Stack Overflow built as a full-stack technical exercise. The goal was to implement the core platform features — questions, answers, votes, tags, profiles, collections — using the modern Next.js 16 App Router stack with MongoDB, and add an original feature: AI-assisted answer generation via OpenAI GPT.
suggestedCaseStudyText.learnings: The project required tackling real problems that rarely surface in tutorials: persisting users in MongoDB inside NextAuth v5's async callbacks, using Mongoose transactions to guarantee consistency during OAuth signup, and building per-user rate limiting without external dependencies. Integrating Tiptap v3 (then in beta) required custom extensions for features not yet stable like inline code highlight.
suggestedCaseStudyText.particularAspects: The most interesting part is the AI integration: the API generates native HTML compatible with Tiptap (not Markdown), respects and improves the user's existing draft, and is protected by an atomic rate limit stored on MongoDB with compensating rollback on provider error. The OAuth flow uses Mongoose transactions to create user and account atomically, with automatic unique username generation via iterative slug.
suggestedCaseStudyText.outcome: A deployed, working application with multi-provider auth, a rich text editor with syntax highlighting, vote/save system, server-side search and filters, pagination, and AI answer generation with rate limiting. The codebase follows scalable patterns: typed Server Actions, a generic DataRenderer, end-to-end schema validation with Zod.

title: Trance Travel
shortDescription: Full-stack AI web app that generates personalized travel itineraries enriched with images, Stripe payments, and an admin dashboard.
fullDescription: Trance Travel is a full-stack web app dedicated to creating personalized travel itineraries via generative AI. Users choose destination, duration, budget, travel style, interests, and group type. The system sends these preferences to DeepSeek and generates a structured itinerary with description, estimated price, weather, best travel periods, and day-by-day activities. The project also includes a personal area, trip payment flow, and an admin dashboard.
problem: Building a full product around generative AI requires more than a single API call — it involves prompt design, structured output parsing, database persistence, and integrating external services like payments and image APIs into a coherent user experience.
features: AI itinerary generation with day-by-day breakdown via DeepSeek
Filterable ComboBoxes and interactive Syncfusion world map for country selection
Stripe payment flow with confetti success page
Admin dashboard with stats, charts, and generated trips table
projectType: AI Travel Web App / Admin Dashboard
stackSummary: React Router v7 in framework mode with server-side loaders and actions, Prisma and PostgreSQL for data persistence, Better Auth for Google login, and DeepSeek Chat Completions for structured itinerary generation from user preferences.
whatILearned: Integrating generative AI into a real application flow, from user data collection to structured itinerary generation.
Writing prompts oriented toward obtaining consistent, reusable JSON output from an LLM.
Handling AI response parsing and validation before saving to the database.
Combining AI-generated content with Unsplash images and Stripe payment links.
Building a complete full-stack experience with authentication, database, admin dashboard, and AI generation.

particularAspects.title: Trip generator
particularAspects.content: Generative AI pipeline that creates day-by-day itineraries based on destination, duration, budget, interests, travel style, and group type.

particularAspects.title: Structured prompts
particularAspects.content: Prompt engineering designed to extract structured data: title, description, estimated price, weather, best time to visit, and daily activities.

particularAspects.title: End-to-end flow
particularAspects.content: End-to-end AI pipeline: input form → DeepSeek call → JSON parsing → Prisma save → detail page rendering.

particularAspects.title: Stripe checkout
particularAspects.content: Each AI-generated trip is enriched with Unsplash images and linked to a Stripe payment flow.

designFocus: Travel-oriented UI with large imagery, destination cards, colored pills, and responsive layout.
Clean palette with primary blue, light backgrounds, soft shadows, and generous border radius.
Distinct navigation layers for public site, personal area, and admin dashboard.
Empty state pages for featured trips and personal trips sections.
developmentFocus: Separate route architecture for public site, admin dashboard, and API actions.
Prisma data model covering users, sessions, auth accounts, and generated trips.
Isolated server functions for trips, dashboard stats, auth helpers, and Stripe.
Client/server validation for generation limits, trip duration, and authentication.
interactionDetails: Filterable ComboBoxes for country, travel style, interests, budget, and group type.
Syncfusion world map that highlights the selected country in real time.
Animated loader shown during AI itinerary generation.
Confetti animation on the payment success page.
technicalHighlights: DeepSeek Chat Completions integration for generating personalized itineraries in structured JSON format.
Robust AI response parsing that handles output even when wrapped in markdown code blocks.
Per-user generation cap of 3 trips to prevent excessive AI and image API usage.
Generated itineraries stored in the database as serialized JSON for fast retrieval.
Dynamic rendering of AI output across cards, detail pages, itinerary lists, and the admin dashboard.
portfolioValue: The project is particularly strong in a portfolio because it shows real-world use of generative AI inside a full-stack product. It is not just an isolated API call: the AI enters a complete flow with user input, structured generation, persistence, rendering, images, payment, and admin dashboard.

suggestedCaseStudyText.overview: Trance Travel is a full-stack web app dedicated to creating personalized travel itineraries via generative AI. The user can choose destination, duration, budget, travel style, interests, and group type. The system sends these preferences to DeepSeek and generates a structured itinerary with description, estimated price, weather, recommended periods, and day-by-day activities. The project also includes a personal area, trip payment, and an admin dashboard.
suggestedCaseStudyText.learnings: Building the project involved working on a complete generative AI flow applied to a real product. I learned to design prompts for reusable JSON output, handle AI response parsing, and save itineraries to the database. I integrated this logic with authentication, external images, Stripe payments, and admin views — demonstrating both frontend and backend competency.
suggestedCaseStudyText.particularAspects: One of the most interesting aspects is the AI pipeline: user form, DeepSeek call, structured output, persistence, and rendering in the UI. Each generated trip is displayed with a gallery, information chips, daily schedule, weather, and best travel period. Country selection uses a filterable ComboBox and a Syncfusion world map. The admin dashboard adds a management view with statistics, charts, and tables.
suggestedCaseStudyText.outcome: The result is a demonstrative but complete web app, well-suited for showing the practical use of generative AI in a full-stack context. In the portfolio it communicates the ability to design UI, manage data, integrate external services, and turn AI output into a concrete product experience.
